gloss: view of life and death; philosophy on mortality

definitions.gloss: view of life and death; attitude toward life and death; philosophy on mortality
definitions.explanation: One's personal or cultural perspective on the meaning of life and death, including how one faces mortality and what significance one assigns to living and dying.

examples.japanese: {死生観|しせいかん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{人|ひと}それぞれ→人それぞれ：24844_hitosorezore⟧だ。
examples.english: Everyone has their own view of life and death.

examples.japanese: ⟦{病気|びょうき}→病気：00771_byouki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{経験|けいけん}→経験：01179_keiken⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧{死生観|しせいかん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{変|か}わった→変わる：00714_kawaru⟧。
examples.english: My view of life and death changed after experiencing illness.

examples.japanese: ⟦{武士道|ぶしどう}→武士道：17460_bushidou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{独自|どくじ}→独自：05614_dokuji⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{死生観|しせいかん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦あり→ある：00006_aru⟧、⟦{死|し}→死：13248_shi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{恐|おそ}れ→恐れる：02023_osoreru⟧ず⟦{生|い}きる→生きる：01184_ikiru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{美徳|びとく}→美徳：13899_bitoku⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Bushido had its own philosophy on life and death, in which living without fear of death was considered a virtue.

notes:
A compound of {死生|しせい} (life and death) and {観|かん} (view, perspective). This is a culturally significant concept in Japanese thought, deeply influenced by Buddhism, Shinto, and the samurai tradition. Discussions of {死生観|しせいかん} are common in literature, philosophy, religion, and end-of-life care contexts.

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, the concept of {死生観|しせいかん} often comes up in discussions about ⟦{終活|しゅうかつ}→終活：27374_shuukatsu⟧ (end-of-life preparation), ⟦{看取|みと}り→看取る：20215_mitoru⟧ (attending a dying person), and traditional arts like ⟦{茶道|さどう}→茶道：04451_sadou⟧ (tea ceremony), which incorporate awareness of impermanence (⟦{無常|むじょう}→無常：13422_mujou⟧).
